Changelog

ididvar (development version)

Breaking changes

  • idid_to_cf() (“idid to control form”) now returns the control form of a regression (an idid_cf object), an equivalent linear regression, instead of a re-estimated model. It supports lm, glm, fixest, AER::ivreg, plm and felm. The regression can be refitted from it, which gives back its coefficients but not its standard errors:

    reg_cf <- idid_to_cf(reg)
stats::lm.wfit(reg_cf$x, reg_cf$y, reg_cf$weights)$coefficients

# with fixed effects
fixest::feols.fit(reg_cf$y, reg_cf$x,
  fixef_df = as.data.frame(reg_cf$fixef_id), weights = reg_cf$weights)

  • Variables of interest must be coefficients of the regression (eg "treat:post"), or variables matching one (eg "x" for "fit_x" in a fixest IV).

  • idid_partial_out() and idid_weights() no longer re-estimate the model, so ... is not used anymore.

New features

  • idid_share_var() returns the share of the variance of a variable (the outcome or a variable of interest) removed by partialling out the controls.

Bug fixes

  • idid_partial_out() partials out the controls of the regression as estimated. Controls dropped by the regression are no longer partialled out, and GLMs, IVs with transformed variables or missing values, plm models estimated on unsorted data, interactions and weighted regressions work.
  • Models estimated inside a function now work. An error is raised if the data has been modified since estimation.
  • idid_drop_change() now works with an exogenous variable of interest in an IV and with coefficient names containing parentheses or dots (eg log(x)).
  • Effective sample (idid_drop_reg(), idid_drop_change(), idid_contrib_threshold() and the functions using them):
    • the threshold corresponds to the last step that does not change the estimate by more than threshold_change, not the first one that does. Observations with a weight equal to the threshold now contribute.
    • only observations of the estimation sample are dropped, and observations with the same weight are all dropped or all kept.
    • idid_drop_change() returns one row per variable of interest. The search requires every one of them to pass.
    • a regression that fails after dropping observations counts as a large change instead of stopping the search.
    • standard errors come from vcov(). For fixest, both use the variance of the regression passed (eg clustering set in summary()) and no small sample correction.
    • idid_drop_change() gains a vcov argument, a function computing the variance of both regressions (eg sandwich::vcovHC). It can be passed to the other functions through ....
    • felm and glm work, and fixest notes are not repeated.
    • idid_viz_drop_change() uses search_step.
